candidate_relations.reason: Granuloma annulare has a granulomatous histopathologic pattern, unlike the eosinophil-rich perivascular and interstitial inflammation supporting eosinophilic annular erythema.

Contact dermatitis implies an external contact trigger and typically eczematous features; the record instead describes non-scaly annular plaques with numerous eosinophils and no stated contact exposure.
Immune-mediated dermatitis could broadly encompass a checkpoint-inhibitor-associated eruption but omits the specific diagnosis of eosinophilic annular erythema.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Broad inflammatory and possible treatment-related category

candidate_relations.reason: Sweet syndrome classically presents with tender plaques and dense neutrophilic inflammation, not the pruritic annular plaques with prominent eosinophils shown here.
Dermatitis is too broad and does not preserve the required specific clinicopathologic diagnosis of eosinophilic annular erythema.
